items.note: Soil of the district is generally black cotton soil (mar), rich and very good for wheat but reduced in utility if kans grows.

The duab between the Bah and the Betwa is the richest cultivated area of Vidisha tahsil; the central tract is rich from silt deposits and a major wheat-growing district of the erstwhile Gwalior State.
Vidisha is predominantly a rabi crop area (65:35 in 1971-72); wheat commands 50 per cent of cropped area, then gram and jowar.
Agricultural operations follow the rainfall in the manner of the Malwa tract: fields broken with the bakhar, ploughing for autumn crops about the end of May, sowing after sufficient rain.
